title: Choose FinVault's look
question: The Securo look is out. The roll dealt Survey Sheet. Keep it, take an alternate, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Survey Sheet
options.lineage: Canadian topographic map sheets: the collar, the legend, the grid and the gazetteer
options.thesis: Your household's money drawn as a map sheet: income runs downstream into categories, each import re-surveys the sheet.
options.viewport: The sheet collar names the household and month with an edition stamp; a watershed of this month's money flows from income to categories; the gazetteer of transactions sits beneath, Import survey at top right.
options.risk: The map metaphor could obscure plain answers; tables and totals must stay literal and legible.

raised.raise: Every sheet has a keyed number and the whole app runs from the keyboard: 1 overview, 2 accounts, 3 gazetteer, i to import.
Selecting a category or column pulls its figures into focus while the rest of the sheet drops back.
Controls have real pressed states: a toggle visibly sinks into the collar when active.
One axis rules every line: time runs down the gazetteer and across every chart in the same direction.

regions.label: sheet collar: household · month · edition · Import survey

options.label: Sorting Case
options.lineage: The post office sorting case and the postmark on every statement that used to arrive by mail
options.thesis: Each statement arrives, gets postmarked with its dates, and every line is sorted into its pigeonhole.
options.viewport: A wall of category pigeonholes filling as the newest statement is sorted; unsorted lines wait in the tray at left.
options.risk: Leans on postal imagery; must stay generic, never any postal service's own marks.

options.label: Season Folio
options.lineage: A botanical folio: one plant, every stage, same scale and ground
options.thesis: Every month drawn as a plate at the same scale, so months compare at a glance.
options.viewport: Twelve month plates on one baseline, the current month open with its categories annotated.
options.case: Holds product clarity (fixed-scale months make comparison honest) but loses audience identification.
options.risk: Cream ground and engraved captions are the most common look in this kind of redesign.

options.label: Teletext Pages
options.thesis: Every screen a three-digit page on black.
options.viewport: P100 index, accounts as numbered rows.
options.case: Loses both axes: dense and cold for this household.
options.kept: Keyboard-first: every page is keyed directly.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.viewport: A wall of bars per transaction.
options.case: Loses both axes: clinical and dense.
options.kept: Selection pulls one column into focus.

options.label: CD-ROM Console
options.thesis: A rendered console around a small window.
options.viewport: Console frame, content in a small window.
options.case: Loses both axes: novelty that shrinks the data.

options.label: Deep Dive
options.case: Loses both axes: atmosphere over data.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean personal-finance dashboard, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, headline totals, cards of charts and recent transactions.
canonCard.risk: This is the Securo-style look you just rejected; every finance app looks like this.
